knowledge_sample: [{category:"SOC",title:"Security Operations Center",difficulty:"beginner",content:"A SOC is a centralized facility where a team of security professionals monitors, detects, analyzes, and responds to cybersecurity incidents. SOC teams use SIEM, EDR, and other tools to maintain visibility across the organization's infrastructure. Key roles include SOC Analyst (L1-L3), SOC Manager, Threat Hunter, and Incident Responder.",keyPoints:["24/7 monitoring capability","Tiered analyst structure (L1-L3)","Uses SIEM, SOAR, and EDR tools","Focuses on detection and response"]},{category:"SIEM",title:"Security Information & Event Management",difficulty:"beginner",content:"SIEM systems collect, aggregate, and analyze log data from across an organization's technology infrastructure. They provide real-time monitoring, event correlation, alerting, and compliance reporting. Modern SIEMs include user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) for advanced threat detection.",keyPoints:["Log collection and normalization","Real-time correlation and alerting","Compliance reporting","UEBA and analytics"]},{category:"EDR",title:"Endpoint Detection & Response",difficulty:"intermediate",content:"EDR solutions continuously monitor endpoint activities including process execution, file operations, registry changes, and network connections. They use behavioral analysis to detect threats that bypass traditional antivirus, providing investigation and response capabilities directly on the endpoint.",keyPoints:["Continuous endpoint monitoring","Behavioral threat detection","Forensic investigation tools","Automated response actions"]},{category:"XDR",title:"Extended Detection & Response",difficulty:"intermediate",content:"XDR extends detection and response across multiple security layers — endpoints, email, network, cloud, and identity. By correlating signals from diverse sources, XDR provides a unified view of threats and automates response across the entire security stack.",keyPoints:["Cross-layer correlation","Unified security visibility","Automated response orchestration","Reduced alert fatigue"]},{category:"MITRE ATT&CK",title:"MITRE ATT&CK Framework",difficulty:"intermediate",content:"MITRE ATT&CK is a globally-accessible knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques based on real-world observations. It provides a common framework for describing attacker behavior, helping organizations assess their security posture, identify detection gaps, and evaluate security tools.",keyPoints:["14 enterprise tactics","200+ techniques and sub-techniques","Maps adversary behavior","Guides detection engineering"]},{category:"Incident Response",title:"Incident Response Process",difficulty:"intermediate",content:"IR follows a structured lifecycle: Preparation → Detection & Analysis → Containment → Eradication → Recovery → Lessons Learned. Each phase has specific objectives, procedures, and deliverables. Playbooks provide standardized response procedures for common incident types.",keyPoints:["6-phase lifecycle","Playbook-driven response","Evidence preservation","Post-incident review"]},{category:"Threat Intelligence",title:"Cyber Threat Intelligence",difficulty:"advanced",content:"CTI is the collection, analysis, and dissemination of information about current and potential threats. It includes strategic (high-level trends), tactical (TTPs), operational (campaigns), and technical (IOCs) intelligence. CTI feeds into detection rules, hunting hypotheses, and risk assessments.",keyPoints:["Strategic, tactical, operational, technical levels","IOC and TTP analysis","Threat actor profiling","Integration with SIEM and SOAR"]},{category:"Digital Forensics",title:"Digital Forensics Fundamentals",difficulty:"advanced",content:"Digital forensics involves the identification, preservation, analysis, and presentation of digital evidence. Key areas include disk forensics, memory forensics, network forensics, and mobile forensics. Chain of custody and evidence integrity are critical for legal proceedings.",keyPoints:["Evidence preservation and integrity","Memory and disk analysis","Timeline reconstruction","Chain of custody documentation"]},{category:"Cloud Security",title:"Cloud Security Operations",difficulty:"intermediate",content:"Cloud security involves protecting data, applications, and infrastructure in cloud environments. Key considerations include shared responsibility models, IAM policies, network security groups, encryption, logging (CloudTrail, Azure Monitor), and compliance frameworks specific to cloud deployments.",keyPoints:["Shared responsibility model","IAM and least privilege","Cloud-native logging","Compliance in the cloud"]},{category:"Zero Trust",title:"Zero Trust Architecture",difficulty:"advanced",content:"Zero Trust eliminates implicit trust by continuously verifying every user, device, and application regardless of location. Core principles: never trust, always verify; least privilege access; assume breach. Implementation requires strong identity verification, micro-segmentation, and continuous monitoring.",keyPoints:["Never trust, always verify","Micro-segmentation","Continuous authentication","Least privilege enforcement"]}]
